title: Gate an advisory all-clear on a positive health condition
statement: A priority-ordered recommendation ladder ending in a green 'everything is fine' card will reassure the user about a broken system whenever no specific rule happened to match. Gate the all-clear on a positive health condition and return nothing otherwise. Time-bound every 'live' finding, and count only currently-open problems when estimating a current rate.

title: De-duplicate alerts with a durable episode row per subject
statement: State-crossing alerts ('became unhealthy', 'recovered') must fire once per episode, not once per failing event, and must survive process restarts. Keep one durable episode row per subject: emit on the crossing into breach, no-op while the episode is open, emit once on the crossing back and close it. Keeping the state in a table rather than memory is what makes restart-safety free.

title: Alert evaluation must not live in the tab that displays alerts
statement: If the only place rules are evaluated is the observability screen's data hook, alerts fire only while that screen is open. Move evaluation to an always-mounted background service, give it its own small snapshot fetch so it never clobbers the filtered state the screen is showing, and guard overlapping ticks so two passes can't race past the cooldown and double-fire.

title: Smooth a noisy metric, then band it with two-threshold hysteresis
statement: A gauge driven straight off raw samples flickers at every band boundary. Run the sample through an EMA to damp single-tick spikes, then use separate ENTER and EXIT thresholds per level — a metric must cross the higher threshold to worsen and fall below the lower one to recover. The gap between them is the anti-flicker.

title: Health checks must PROBE, not infer
statement: Round-trip a throwaway keyring entry and do a TEMP-table write to prove the DB is writable rather than inferring health from configuration; each failing item ships its remediation.

title: Keep a bounded stderr ring so a timeout is diagnosable
statement: Keep a 32KB stderr tail with char-boundary truncation and append it to the returned error, so a timed-out subprocess run is diagnosable after the fact.

title: Add a new liveness signal as corroboration that degrades to the old rule
statement: When adding a new health signal to an existing liveness/staleness decision, wire it as corroboration only — it may veto or confirm the incumbent rules but never replaces a trigger — and make every rule fall back to exactly the pre-signal behaviour whenever the new evidence is unusable.

title: Capture timeout diagnostics inside the wait primitive itself, with a content-free shape for shareable logs
statement: A wait/expect primitive should attach evidence (screen snapshot, raw tail, generation, lifecycle state, and an 'ended' flag distinguishing dead-target from unresponsive-target) at the moment of timeout — and expose a content-free summary for logs that must not carry user data, verified by a test.

title: Flag reconstructed telemetry as synthetic and badge it, never present estimates as measurements
statement: When a trace/timeline is reconstructed from coarse endpoints instead of captured live, mark the reconstructed object with an explicit `isSynthetic` flag and have every renderer show an 'Estimated' badge — millisecond-precision guesses presented as fact mislead operators. Note that live vs synthetic are independent axes: a historical execution can have a real captured trace (neither), and a synthetic trace is never the live one.

title: Audit why an automation cascade did NOT continue, one structured row per non-continuation
statement: Every non-continuation path in a chained-automation evaluator (suppressed handoff, cycle skip, depth ceiling, unmet predicate, quarantine, cost ceiling, healing abandonment) should write a structured stop-reason row keyed by the distributed trace id — machine reason token + human detail + depth — so an operator can answer 'why did this chain stop?'. Writes are best-effort: a lost audit row must never fail the cascade. Whole-cascade halts carry NULL trigger references since they aren't tied to one link.

title: Presence from an append-only feed: time-bound the working state, leave the waiting state unbounded
statement: Deriving liveness ('working' / 'waiting') from a paged event feed must acknowledge that the terminal row clearing a state may simply never arrive (crash, cancel, machine sleep). So 'working' holds only while the latest step_running row is fresher than the runner's own liveness horizon; 'waiting on a human' is DELIBERATELY unbounded because a review gate legitimately holds for hours and remains true until someone acts. Pick the freshness window from the producer's heartbeat cadence, not an arbitrary number.

title: Never drop a stream line silently — an empty terminal envelope must name its subtype
statement: In a stream-json parser, every line the model actually emitted must surface somewhere. Valid-JSON-but-not-an-object lines become progress entries rather than being dropped, and a terminal `result` envelope that carries no text (error_max_turns, error_during_execution) must emit a message naming the subtype — otherwise a turn that BROKE looks identical to a turn that simply had nothing to add.

title: A failed run is a completed observation; an unfinished row stays running — a ledger must not guess between them
statement: Every cap, truncation, refused id and malformed input is counted into stats and rendered into a 'what I did not see, and what I dropped' section of the human report. A failed run finishes as failed with the reason inside stats and still writes its report; an unfinished row is deliberately left running forever, because 'the process died' and 'still working' are different facts the ledger must not conflate.

title: Instrument pool acquires with a labeled starvation threshold, and convert acquire hangs into recoverable errors
statement: Give the connection pool a hard acquire timeout (a frozen worker becomes a recoverable error instead of a hung UI) and a drop-in instrumented acquire that logs caller label, wait time, and pool state whenever a successful acquire exceeded a tuned starvation threshold — so pool contention is visible in production logs, swappable at hot paths without other changes.

title: Assert cross-table data invariants at startup — loud error log, never a crash
statement: After migrations, run cheap SQL assertions of the invariants your migration chain is supposed to guarantee (e.g. 'no row holds both the legacy blob and the new field rows'). Log violations at error level with the offending ids for forensics, but do not abort boot — a transient inconsistency during a future migration may be acceptable, while a silent one regresses undetected.

title: A red fleet indicator needs both a minimum terminal sample and a strict-majority ratio
statement: A user-facing 'failure spike' alarm should fire only when BOTH hold: the terminal sample (completed+failed, excluding in-flight and cancelled) meets a minimum count, AND failures are a strict majority of finished runs. Either alone is noise: a single bad run on a quiet morning paints the fleet red; a large sample at exactly 50% is ambiguous. Capture thresholds as named exported constants with per-constant rationale and a boundary-behavior table, and state the denominator doctrine at module top so every ratio in the file shares it.

title: Give the recorder a signature that cannot fail the work
statement: Instrumentation that can fail the work it measures is worse than no instrumentation. Give the recorder a signature that cannot propagate failure — return `Option<Id>` and log a warning instead of `Result` — parse the source event tolerantly with every field optional, and let a missing measurement record a row with NULLs rather than skipping the row. The event still happened; only the numbers are unknown.

title: Count the swallows inside the helper, not at the call sites
statement: When a codebase routes intentional error-swallowing through one helper, make that helper count. Aggregate swallows per call-site tag, emit a periodic rollup (one structured log + one breadcrumb), and sample a real exception capture for high-frequency tags — so a path that fails 400 times a session becomes a visible issue instead of 400 invisible breadcrumbs. Zero changes at the call sites.

title: Keep a ring for percentiles and lifetime counters for rates
statement: Instrument the transport wrapper itself: record duration/ok/timedOut for every call into a fixed ring for percentiles, but keep never-evicted cumulative counters for the rates — deriving a lifetime rate from a windowed buffer is wrong the moment the window wraps.

title: Generate repository CRUD from macros so every query is timed for free
statement: Express the repetitive repository surface (`get_by_id`, `get_all`, `delete`, partial `update`, row mappers) as declarative macros, and bake the timing call into the generated body. Instrumentation you have to remember to add is instrumentation you will forget; instrumentation the code generator emits is total.

title: Corroborate an idle claim with an artifact the process can't fake
statement: A managed process telling you it is idle is a hint, not a fact. Derive liveness from an independent artifact it produces (log/transcript byte growth, output bytes), snapshot a baseline when the idle claim arrives, and revive the state if the artifact grows past that baseline.

title: Cap slot-to-run matching tolerance at half the neighbour gap
statement: Reconciling a schedule's nominal fire times against real run records needs a tolerance window for tick lateness — but a fixed window lets a fast schedule's slot steal its neighbour's run, and lets a late backfill be misattributed to the slot it was compensating for. Cap the per-slot tolerance at half the distance to each adjacent slot, consume each run at most once (nearest wins), and leave unmatched slots explicitly unknown.

title: Derive stall state from output silence when there is no heartbeat
statement: A long-running job that streams output but sends no heartbeat gives you exactly one liveness signal: the gap since the last line. Track it with graded thresholds (active → waiting → stuck), reset on any new output, and let the UI change what it offers at each level instead of showing an indeterminate spinner forever.

title: Log refused handshakes at warn with the concrete stage and reason
statement: Funnel every handshake rejection path through one logging helper via `.inspect_err(...)`, tagging the stage (incoming Hello / incoming HelloAck / missing HelloConfirm / malformed HelloConfirm) so a misconfigured device is distinguishable from an impersonation attempt.

title: Warn on the crossing, not the level — latch per rejection streak, reset on admission
statement: A guard that rejects high-frequency calls (rate limiter, breaker) must log its warning once per rejection STREAK via a latch, and reset the latch the moment a request is admitted again — otherwise a hammering caller floods the log with one warning per call, or (if never reset) a later independent streak never warns at all.

title: Audit through one chokepoint that counts its own failures
statement: Auditability and availability conflict: if you fail the operation when the audit write fails you cause outages; if you swallow the error you get decrypts with no trail and nobody notices. Take the third path — one append-only insert function that ALL audit writes go through, callers free to ignore its `Result`, but every failure increments a process counter that the product surfaces in its own trust UI. The gap becomes visible instead of silent.

title: Write the audit entry in the repository, not the command handler
statement: Put the audit-log write at the lowest shared layer (the repository function) rather than at the API/IPC boundary. Then internal callers — background ticks, engine subscriptions, an admin HTTP surface — are audited too, at the cost of losing the caller-origin tag. Suppress no-op writes so the history stays signal-rich, and never let an audit failure fail the underlying write.

title: Log through one closed event union, never a bare console call
statement: Make every application event a variant of one closed discriminated union, and allow exactly one logging helper in application code with a lint rule holding the line. Adding an event type then means extending the union first, so the type checker rather than review catches the branch that logs a partial row.

title: Budget threshold warnings per key, and summarise the suppressed
statement: A threshold-triggered warning needs a rate budget, or a retry storm turns your signal into noise and your error tracker into a bill. Budget N warns per key per window; count the suppressed ones and their worst duration, and emit a single summary line when the window rolls.

title: Publish each metric's identity: source, window, computation
statement: The same label ('Success Rate') computed from different sources over different windows is three different metrics. Declare each occurrence as a named identity record carrying source, time window, and computation kind (raw ratio vs precomputed), and resolve the displayed number through one helper that honours the declared kind.

title: Give orphans and collisions their own bucket in every rollup
statement: Aggregations quietly drop rows that don't join: work whose owner was deleted, processes with no attributable entity, entities with no group. Each of those is exactly the signal an operator needs. Emit an explicit orphan/system/ungrouped bucket, and never fall back to matching on a display name unless you've proven it identifies exactly one entity.

title: Prove a composite score's inputs are independent and monotonic
statement: Before shipping a weighted health/quality score, verify that no two sub-scores read the same underlying metric, that every sub-score curve is monotonic in the direction of 'worse', that the weights sum to 1.0 (asserted at module load in dev), and that the arithmetic is pinned by tests. Both failure modes have shipped here and both were invisible until someone did the algebra.

title: Never fabricate a trend from a single loaded window
statement: A prior-period comparison is only real if the series was actually fetched at 2x the window. Splitting one window into front-half/back-half and calling the ratio 'period-over-period change' produces noise that users act on. Enforce the invariant in one splitter that returns null when no genuine prior half exists, and let consumers omit the trend chip.

title: Make 'unknown' a first-class state, distinct from zero and absent
statement: Any surface that reconstructs history or aggregates several independent sources must carry an explicit unknown/stale state and render it, rather than substituting a default that reads as a measured fact. Absence of a record means the observation is missing — never that the thing succeeded, never that the count is zero.

title: Make a self-measuring loop structurally unable to fake a win
statement: Any system that closes its own loop — verify a fix, score a run, report improvement — will drift toward reporting success unless the honesty rules are coded. Three make it hard: require proof the sensor actually ran before absence-of-signal can count as cleared; keep 'unchanged' and 'regressed' as first-class outcomes surfaced as loudly as success; and put a material-improvement noise floor under any numeric claim.

title: Stamp coverage on WHAT WAS READ, not what survived dedup
statement: Coverage reflects what was read; derive pct from counts when given, never invent it; unknown depth is recorded as owing rather than assumed complete.

title: Sample host metrics from ONE long-lived sampler, first sample marked invalid
statement: Recreating the System sampler resets the CPU baseline so it always reads 0%; keep one long-lived sampler, mark the first sample invalid, and never enumerate processes.

title: Write back the REAL outcome of a delegated run
statement: Scheduled automation otherwise records success at request-emit time; write back the delegated run's actual outcome instead.

title: Weight aggregate read-depth by territory size, and return null over an empty denominator
statement: When rolling per-scope coverage into one number, done/total alone lets a corpus skimmed at 11% look finished. Compute the depth figure as a file-count-weighted mean of per-scope read percentages (100% of 100 files must not cancel 10% of 900), exclude scopes that reported no depth rather than assuming them complete, and return null — not 0/0 — when there is nothing to report so the UI stays silent instead of implying 'nothing to do here'.

title: Match a rate's numerator and denominator to the same population and window
statement: A rate computed from mismatched populations lies confidently. Two concrete traps: dividing failures by ALL executions (including running/queued/cancelled) inflates the denominator so error_rate + success_rate no longer sum to 100 and alerts under-fire; and using a lifetime issue tally as the numerator over a windowed execution count marks a currently-healthy worker as failing. Fix by pinning both sides: decided runs only in the denominator, currently-open failures only in the numerator.

title: Never ship a hardcoded constant that renders as a computed metric — measure it, with a minimum-sample floor
statement: A literal like strength: 0.7 displayed on an analytics edge reads as measurement and poisons trust in everything beside it. Replace it with the real computation (here: Jaccard overlap of two series' failure days over their shared window) and give the measurement a minimum-sample floor that returns 0 for 'too little shared history' — one coincident bad day must not print a 1.0 correlation.

title: Age-gate 'live' alerts derived from a retained analytics window
statement: Dashboards retain anomalies across their whole window, so a recommendation engine that surfaces any above-threshold anomaly renders a weeks-old spike as a current critical. Add an explicit recency bound (a few days) on top of the magnitude threshold before an event may masquerade as happening now; older anomalies stay visible in history, not in the 'act on this' slot.

title: Log the intents your matcher could NOT serve, and surface them to the curator
statement: A routing/matching layer over a curated catalog (playbooks, templates, FAQ answers) should persist every unmatched request alongside per-entry match counts — the unmatched list is real-demand evidence of which situation has no catalog entry yet, sourced from actual requests rather than a curator's guess.

title: Learned per-entity thresholds need a sample floor, absolute floors, and 'absent band means unknown, not zero'
statement: Anomaly thresholds computed as 1.5x an entity's own trailing p95 must carry a minimum sample count, absolute floors, and a fall-through to the global constant when the band is absent. The observed trap: a nullable column made percentile([]) == 0 persist as a real p95, collapsing the slow threshold to the floor and flagging everything.

title: Record a failure row for every attempt via an arm/disarm guard, so backpressure is not counted and no attempt counts twice
statement: Every error exit used to return before the ledger write, so the health dashboard reported a perfect error rate by construction (is_error was 0 on all 1,734 rows). A thin wrapper converts any Err into exactly one failure row; an armed bit starts false (lock-skips record nothing) and flips off once the turn writes its own success row. Any system reporting its own reliability needs this shape: the metric must be able to be bad.

title: Stamp ambient write-attribution via task-local plus thread-scope RAII, readable inside database hooks
statement: When a synchronous hook deep in the data layer must know 'which execution caused this write' without threading a parameter through every layer, provide two ambient scopes: a tokio task-local wrapper around the whole run future (visible from any sync code polled by the task) and a thread-scoped RAII guard for spawn_blocking paths. Readers check task scope first, then thread scope, and return None for ordinary user writes — and the known gap (out-of-process writers see no hooks) is documented as an accepted limitation rather than papered over.

title: Guard a derived-score history's integrity: append only real changes, and never fold a new dimension into the composite retroactively
statement: A locally recorded time series of a derived score is only trustworthy if (a) a snapshot is appended only when the readings actually changed — so merely opening the surface never inflates the trend — and (b) newly shipped scored dimensions are deliberately left OUT of the composite at first, because folding a new term in would step-change every subject's score at once and the history would render that as real movement. Ship the dimension visible but unweighted; weight it in a change that says so.

title: Judge a simulation channel by pairing each sim point with its nearest real point and trending the normalized gap
statement: When one measurement channel is ground truth and another is a prediction of it (simulated env, forecast, shadow deployment), express credibility as a per-sim-point gap against the nearest-in-time truth point, normalized by the metric's target span. Never invent a pairing (no truth data → explicit 'insufficient', not a gap of 0); flag a truth partner older than the sim point as STALE (the honest move is a re-measure, not a verdict); and only call a converging/diverging direction with ≥2 normalizable runs separated by an epsilon threshold.

title: Label a non-differentiating metric as tied or unavailable instead of letting it masquerade as ranking signal
statement: When a displayed metric currently cannot differentiate subjects — every row shares one fleet-wide value, or there is no honest prior period for a trend — say so inline (a 'tied' chip with the known limitation, no trend arrow) rather than rendering a column or arrow that looks like signal. Detect the degenerate case from the data itself (a Set of the values has size 1) so the label disappears the day the metric becomes real.
